tasks.short: Review filings to identify issues and grounds for relief

steps.what: Review complaints, petitions, motions and pleadings to determine issues and grounds for relief

tasks.design: Keep substantive filing review and issue identification with the clerk using {DOCS} and original legal sources. The proposal makes no automated application of law to case facts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identifying issues requires understanding allegations, procedural posture and legal context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing documents and source search support manual review.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous pleadings, disputed facts and implicit legal arguments.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk separates allegations from findings and can explain the basis of an issue analysis.

reach.learn: Present uncertainties and alternative readings clearly

evidence.claim: The digest reports that Rechtspraak currently targets low-risk uses and avoids AI in high-risk processes; this supports retaining substantive legal analysis with people.

assumptions: The task is substantive review rather than docket administration or document formatting.
The clerk reads filings and gathers necessary context within s1; all time remains counted without a free issue classification field.
Existing document and source tools suffice before a model.
No new service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which document access obstacles are separable from substantive legal review?

already_counted.description: Read filings, verify context and identify issues

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving. No substantive judicial AI saving is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Track legal changes and inform judges of case implications

steps.what: Define law update subscriptions and verify monitored source coverage
Collect changes in the law through configured source alerts
Read original changes, assess case implications and inform judges

tasks.design: Configure official and licensed source subscriptions in the legal update service {OTHER}, with links delivered through {EMAIL}. The clerk determines legal status and case implications and briefs judges directly; the service performs no case-impact analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly checking the same publication channels for new material.
tasks.enabler_now: Native subscriptions and saved filters can collect source notices.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a change is effective and how it affects a particular case.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk verifies original text and presents qualified implications to the judge.

reach.learn: Check source completeness and version status

evidence.claim: Native source alerts are an E1 design proposal; the digest does not establish measured judicial law-update savings.

assumptions: Only repeated source retrieval changes; interpretation and judge briefings retain full time.
The clerk produces source identifiers, topic filters, frequency and fallback channels in s1; 20 hours include capture and coverage checks. Missing sources or failed feeds are checked manually in s3.
OTHER means legal update subscription service; native alerts precede custom integration or model summaries.
No confidential case facts are sent to alert services and no automatic case-impact field is produced.
research_questions: Do saved alerts retrieve known relevant changes without adding screening time or losing source coverage?

already_counted.description: Source configuration, legal interpretation and judge briefing

incremental.description: Maintain source coverage and check missed updates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80 yields 20 gross less 6 focal upkeep =14 central net. Report 0-3 pending source-check timing; existing alerts or manual coverage requirements can eliminate gains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend hearings and record necessary case information

steps.what: Attend court sessions, hear oral arguments and record necessary case information

tasks.design: Retain hearing attendance, attentive listening and necessary note capture with the clerk using {DOCS}. A transcript is not assumed to replace observing the proceeding or selecting relevant information.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk must follow the proceeding and understand its context as it unfolds.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing note tools support contemporaneous capture.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing argument, clarification, disputed facts and procedural directions.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk notices ambiguity and can ask for clarification through the appropriate court process.

reach.learn: Capture relevant procedural and substantive distinctions

evidence.claim: Manual hearing attendance is an E1 proposal; no measured court-session replacement is established by the digest.

assumptions: The baseline is attendance and necessary capture, not a separate verbatim transcription service.
The clerk produces notes during s1 with all capture time counted; no pre-existing structured hearing summary is assumed.
Existing DOCS suffice before any recording or transcription system.
No new service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Does post-hearing transcription exist as a distinct task rather than simultaneous attendance?

already_counted.description: Listening, contextual understanding and case note capture

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. No attendance or simultaneous note-taking saving is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify dockets, event dates and procedural status before progress review
Display pending litigation by event age and recorded procedural dates
Review litigation progress and investigate apparent delays or missing information

tasks.design: Configure an administrative progress view in the case-management system {OTHER}. It sorts recorded dates and flags missing fields; the clerk determines adequacy of progress and any appropriate follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly assembling dated docket information from several views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case views can sort recorded events without interpreting legal merit.
tasks.still_hard: A long interval may be justified and a recorded date may be incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk checks court directions and procedural context before drawing conclusions.

reach.learn: Keep event provenance and distinguish reminders from judicial decisions

evidence.claim: A configured docket progress dashboard is a proposed deterministic E1 design, not a measured deployment.

assumptions: Automation only assembles date-based views; it does not determine legal deadlines from free text, prioritize merits or direct case outcomes.

In s1 the clerk produces case identifier, event type, event date, court-recorded next date, status and source reference; 35 hours include capture and correction. Missing or disputed dates go to manual review in s3.
OTHER means case-management system; native views precede custom dashboards.
Dated status rules only control display of recorded administrative dates and require no automatic legal interpretation.
research_questions: Can the view reproduce a checked docket sample while exposing every absent or disputed event date?

already_counted.description: Field verification, capture and substantive progress review

incremental.description: Maintain view rules and audit missing docket events
Maintain access controls and view integrity

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=70 gives 30 gross less 8 focal upkeep =22 central net. Report 0-5 pending docket timing; native views may already exist and source repair may consume the proposed saving.

reach: Learn source coverage checks from legal librarians
